question.text: An AIF's obligation to conduct due diligence on its own investors relates to:

answer.text: KYC, AML/CFT compliance, and prevention of circumvention of laws

explanation.text: The Logic: AIFs and their managers are required to carry out specific due diligence on their investors to prevent the facilitation of circumvention of laws, and to maintain written AML/CFT procedures. Distributor good practices include providing investor KYC and AML-CFT documentation to authorities as required. The Trap: Option A reduces the obligation to marketing, which is the opposite of its compliance purpose. Options C and D confuse investor DD with performance assessment or tax planning, neither of which is the basis for the obligation. Note: Investor due diligence is a regulatory obligation grounded in KYC and AML/CFT requirements, not an optional commercial check.
